tasks.short: Verify inventory quantities, values and movements against journal and ledger records.

steps.what: Extract inventory balances and journal movements from the {ERP}.
Export stock quantities, valuations and movements from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Set count coverage, materiality and valuation tests in the inventory test plan.
Observe warehouse counts, inspect stock condition and record test counts.
Reconcile counts, valuation calculations and cut-off movements against ledger balances.
Discuss discrepancies and stock condition with the warehouse manager.
Document the inventory conclusion and submit proposed adjustments for approval.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled extracts from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; deterministic checks on the {DATA_PLATFORM} create a reconciliation and exception register in the {WORKFLOW}. A count-entry form captures physical evidence, while templates in the {DOCS} assemble test plans and conclusions; people assess stock condition, investigate differences and approve adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock codes, units, valuation methods and reporting cut-offs differ between records. Physical existence and recoverable value still require evidence beyond matching balances.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export schedules and reconciliation rules can do most data work. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building mappings, evidence forms and repeatable checks; no model loop is necessary for the proposed scope.
tasks.still_hard: Counts remain physical work. Consignment stock, work in progress, obsolete goods and movements during counts need accounting judgement and reliable operational evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge apparently clean records when stock condition, ownership or warehouse practice contradicts them.

ambition.what: Monthly review of slow-moving stock write-down candidates

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends less time copying records and more time on physical evidence and valuation challenges. They can recommend focused follow-up tests; posting and approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Validate standard inventory costs and explain production-cost differences.
reach.learn: Bills of materials, yield losses, overhead allocation and operational units.

reach.task: Maintain inventory exception trends by location and stock category.
reach.learn: Data lineage, stable stock identifiers and reconciliation control totals.

evidence.claim: Scheduled extracts, keyed matching and arithmetic checks can automate structured inventory reconciliations.
DataSnipper supports evidence extraction and tests of details with team review and sign-off.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported statement tick-and-tie falling from eight to two hours; this vendor case does not establish savings for physical inventory work.
The time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.

assumptions: The company holds material physical inventory and uses an {OPS_SYSTEM} alongside the {ERP}.
This describes in-house accounting or internal assurance; statutory audit responsibilities require separate scoping.
Existing systems support scheduled exports; otherwise extraction needs additional integration work.
The build covers one company and a limited set of inventory sources.
GDPR applies where records identify people. National rules determine whether employee consultation is required; the access range assumes no extended consultation process.
unknowns: Available interfaces, export permissions and stock identifier consistency.
Inventory locations, ownership arrangements and valuation methods.
Who approves test scope, accounting conclusions and adjustments.
Whether national rules or existing employee agreements require consultation.
research_questions: Which reconciliation and count-entry functions can be configured in the existing {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}?
Can a prior period be reconciled with explicit control totals and no unexplained dropped records?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers, duplicate records and unmatched movements.
Maintain stock mappings, valuation rules and cut-off calendars.
Check extract completeness and failed scheduled runs.
Review whether exception thresholds miss material issues.
Maintain access controls and evidence retention.

tasks.short: Report asset utilisation and audit findings to management, and recommend operational or financial changes.

steps.what: Extract asset balances, depreciation and utilisation measures from the {ERP}.
Read audit workpapers and compile findings, evidence and unresolved actions.

loop.input: Approved audit workpapers and prior management actions from the {DOCS}.
loop.output: Findings register with source references, recorded severity and action status.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each finding; validate references and have the accountant check completeness.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; missing references or conflicting findings go to the accountant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative workpapers use varied wording and layouts. Use direct field mapping wherever structured findings already exist.

steps.what: Calculate utilisation ratios, trends and financial effects in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Draft findings, assess recommendations and obtain approval to release the management report.

loop.input: Checked analysis, reviewed findings and the approved report template.
loop.output: Draft report with cited findings, calculated figures and proposed recommendations.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; validate source references. The accountant assesses causes and recommendations; the controller approves release.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per report; unsupported causes or recommendations remain flagged for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle tables and headings, but explaining mixed findings requires contextual writing. Calculations remain deterministic.

steps.what: Present findings, challenge assumptions and agree management actions.
Record agreed owners, deadlines and follow-up dates in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Scheduled data from the {ERP} feeds deterministic metrics in the {BI}, while bounded extraction turns workpapers in the {DOCS} into a referenced findings register. A report generator combines fixed tables with bounded narrative drafting, routes release approval through the {WORKFLOW}, and creates records in the {PROJECT} from approved management actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures and narrative findings sit in different places, while reports depend on manual assembly and contextual explanation. Recommendations cannot be accepted through arithmetic checks alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured data feeds and reusable calculations remove repeated preparation. Bounded extraction and drafting can now handle varied workpapers, with source checks and human review.
tasks.still_hard: Utilisation measures may be incomplete or incomparable. Explaining causes, challenging management and choosing changes require operational knowledge and credible relationships.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a weak metric from a real business problem, and persuade management to accept a practical response.

ambition.what: Monthly asset redeployment review with costed options

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends more of the week testing recommendations with operational managers and following their outcomes. They gain capacity to propose options; management retains investment and operating decisions.

reach.task: Compare asset redeployment, replacement and disposal options.
reach.learn: Capital allocation, option costs and operational constraints.

reach.task: Translate accepted audit recommendations into budget changes.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, benefit timing and how to distinguish savings from avoided costs.

evidence.claim: Asset ratios, comparison tables and approved-action routing can use deterministic calculations and configured workflows.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts financial narratives from structured analysis, documents and a template; this supports the drafting pattern, not this exact management-report workflow.
DataSnipper's documented Baker Tilly Netherlands case reports faster statement checking, supporting automation of report verification rather than management judgement.
The digest's spreadsheet benchmark example supports checking generated financial outputs against deterministic control totals.
The time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.

assumptions: The {ERP} holds usable asset records and some utilisation measures; additional operational feeds are outside the base estimate.
Workpapers have stable references and accessible text.
Approved actions can be entered as structured fields after the management discussion.
The build covers one report family and existing access roles.
GDPR applies to personal data in workpapers. National rules determine employee consultation requirements; extended consultation could exceed the estimated range.
unknowns: Which utilisation measures exist and who validates their definitions.
Whether audit workpapers contain structured findings that remove the need for extraction.
Who approves report release and each class of management action.
Whether report access exposes employee-level findings or requires consultation.
research_questions: Which existing {BI} reports and {WORKFLOW} approvals can be reused?
Can reviewers trace every report figure and material claim to an approved source?
new_work: Review extracted findings for omissions and misleading summaries.
Check narrative claims, recommendations and source references.
Maintain metric definitions, report templates and bounded-loop instructions.
Resolve failed data refreshes and changed document structures.
Track whether agreed actions delivered their expected benefits.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling evidence and reports toward investigating exceptions and evaluating operational choices. Professional accountability remains with people, and decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Cost estimation: understand how physical operations create inventory values.
Budget analysis: turn accepted recommendations into funded changes.
Financial management: compare asset options and evaluate realised benefits.
Business intelligence: maintain traceable metrics and reliable evidence links.
skills_to_grow: Inventory valuation and physical evidence assessment
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring asset assurance and redeployment review that combines inventory exceptions, utilisation trends and costed management options.
